dilemma: My parents expect me to take the graduate job. I've been offered a year on a research expedition instead.
neitherReflection: Neither life is yours, which is the point. What you measured them by is what you value.

paths.label: Take the voyage
paths.reflection: You value the story you'll get to tell over the approval you'd get now, and you're betting the door back stays open.

events.title: The offer
events.body: Invited, aged 22, to sail as naturalist on HMS Beagle. His father calls it a waste of time.

events.title: He goes
events.body: His uncle Josiah Wedgwood talks his father round. The Beagle leaves Plymouth.

events.title: Galápagos
events.body: Notes that mockingbirds differ from island to island.

events.title: Home, known
events.body: Returns after five years, already known among naturalists.

events.title: The book
events.body: Publishes On the Origin of Species, 28 years after saying yes.

paths.label: Keep the job
paths.reflection: You value compounding: a steady base you can build the interesting thing on, on your own schedule.

events.title: The steady job
events.body: Becomes a junior clerk at the General Post Office, aged 19.

events.title: Writes before work
events.body: Publishes his first novel while keeping the day job.

events.title: Pillar boxes
events.body: Trials Britain's first roadside post boxes, in Jersey.

events.title: Barchester Towers
events.body: His breakout novel. Still at the Post Office.

events.title: Leaves on his terms
events.body: Resigns after 33 years, now a famous novelist.
